body:
### What are you really trying to do?

We are migrating some flows into Temporal which require tracing, especially for monitoring time spent on certain actions and latency.

### Describe the bug

During testing we noticed that traces for some workflows occasionally contained spans from unrelated activity executions belonging to other workflows. 

This only occurs when untraced workflows (ie, executed without traceparent headers, like when fired from a Schedule) were being executed after workflows that did have a trace associated (traceparent present).

Activities from those untraced workflows may end up generating spans and being attached to the trace of a previously executed workflow.

From our investigation this appears to be caused by the OpenTelemetry context not being properly detached after being attached. The interceptor uses `OpenTelemetry::Context.attach`, but the corresponding `Context.detach(token)` is not always called (see [OTeL spec](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/context/#attach-context) and [api](https://www.rubydoc.info/gems/opentelemetry-api/OpenTelemetry/Context#attach-class_method)).

Because worker threads/fibers are reused, the attached context can remain active and be reused by subsequent workflow/activity executions.

### Minimal Reproduction
* Configure a client and worker with OpenTelemetryInterceptor (and run an OTeL collector)
* Limit activity concurrency to 2 in the worker configuration.
* Create a simple workflow that calls an activity which performs a no-op (or `sleep`).
* Modify the `ClientOutbound` in the `OpenTelemetryInterceptor` to avoid generating a span automatically
   * Without this, all workflow executions are generated with a span on the client side (so, with a traceparent set)
* Execute the workflow several times (ex, +4). 
   * Once inside a span (so a traceparent is set)
   * The following times outside any span (so a traceparent is null).

### Observed behaviour
If the worker reuses the same thread for activity execution, activities belonging to workflows started without tracing may still produce spans and attach to the trace created by the previous workflow execution.

This results in spans from unrelated workflows appearing in the same distributed trace.
title: [Bug] OTeL trace context leaking between workflows when threads/fibers are reused
